# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-14

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely good — I understand what Carnot does in one sentence and
how to install it. But I'd start bouncing the moment I scroll into "Evidence":
twelve cards of unexplained acronyms (FoVer, SVAMP, VeriCoT, CCTU, CRANE,
HalluGuard, PRM-BiasBench, "k=5") with several suspiciously perfect numbers and
one baseline (0.125 AUC) that's literally worse than a coin flip. The page earns
trust in the first screen and then spends it on insider noise.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. The "Evidence / What we measured" results grid is a 12-card jargon wall a
   stranger cannot parse — every card assumes I know a benchmark or method name.
2. Credibility-damaging numbers: a 0.125 AUC "baseline" (below random),
   multiple perfect scores (1.0 TP rate, 60/60, "identical losses") with no
   sample sizes, and a null result ("0.0pp delta") painted with a 95.6% green
   success bar.
3. The hero leads with vanity/insider metrics (3,540 runs, 382 milestones,
   30,658 tests) and jams a changelog-style card ("Repinned from v2 0.9857 …
   architecture-only 0.8947 … 5-seed dual-condition") into the stat row.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Nav bar — 12 text links + 2 buttons (Get Started, Tutorial, Concepts, API,
  Problem, Capabilities, Results, Quick Start, Report, Paper, Writing, Roadmap)
  — cap at ~5-6. A stranger reads none of 12; it signals "we couldn't decide
  what matters."
- Results grid — 12 cards in one section — suggest ≤6 headline cards. The
  rubric's "skim none of them" effect kicks in well before 20 when every card
  needs decoding.
- "Recent progress" card (hero stats) — ~60 words crammed into the stat row,
  doing the job of a changelog — cut to one sentence or move out of the hero.
- Results section intro paragraph — ~60 words of defensive methodology
  ("synthetic-pilot … labeled by provenance … not model-generation headline
  claims") — reads like internal disclaimer, not landing copy; trim to one line.
- Total card load across page: ~4 how-it-works + 7 capabilities + 12 results +
  7 blog = 30 cards. Cumulatively exhausting even though no single section
  exceeds its cap.

### Internal jargon
- Results card "Math reasoning" — "EstimationVerifier SVAMP AUC", "0.125 FoVer
  baseline" — a stranger knows none of EstimationVerifier, SVAMP, or FoVer, and
  can't tell if FoVer is a benchmark, a baseline, or a competitor.
- Results card "Math extraction" — "VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix", "GSM8K
  extraction TP rate" — VeriCoT, GSM8K, "TP rate", "CoT" all unexplained.
- Results card "Adversarial audit" — "PRM-BiasBench-style attacks", "k=5
  ensemble" — PRM, BiasBench, and "k=5" mean nothing to an outsider.
- Results card "Cascade routing — HalluGuard v3" — "HalluGuard v3" is an
  internal component name with a version number.
- Results cards "Ising-guided fuzzing", "CRANE vs rigid grammar", "CCTU
  constrained micro-benchmark" — Ising, CRANE, CCTU all undefined.
- Results card "Safety" — "0.91 AUROC (publication gate)" — "publication gate"
  is internal process vocabulary.
- Hero stats card — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947",
  "Repinned from v2 0.9857" — pure internal methodology/version chatter.
- Capabilities "Multi-step reasoning" — "AND-composed" — jargon.
- Capabilities "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM" — "Process-Reward Energy Model
  (PREM) variance … intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — the
  most opaque + hype-laden card on the page; an outsider gets nothing concrete.
- Capabilities "APIs & portable memory" — "VerdictRecord", "SessionMemory" are
  code identifiers leaked into prose.
- Blog teaser "Five FATAL Findings …" — "Deep Think Rounds" is insider naming
  (acceptable-ish in a blog title, but still unexplained).

### Per-milestone narrative
- No raw "exp1234" or ".148"-style milestone tokens remain in prose — this has
  been cleaned up and is a real improvement.
- Residual narrative flavor: hero card "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after
  pre-submission adversarial audit" reads like a changelog entry, and the
  "382 Completed milestones" stat surfaces the internal milestone concept as a
  vanity number.

### Inconsistencies
- "FoVer" is used two incompatible ways: the hero headline calls 0.9131 the
  AUROC *on* FoVer (FoVer = the benchmark), while the Math-reasoning result
  card calls 0.125 the "FoVer baseline" (FoVer = a competing method). Same word,
  two meanings, on the same page.
- "Seven capabilities … What you can check" but 3 of the 7 cards are not things
  you check: "Research operations" (the dev loop), "APIs & portable memory"
  (integration surfaces), and "Test-Time Compute & PREM" (a budget controller).
  The section header over-promises a taxonomy the cards don't deliver.
- "Why Energy-Based?" says the math "is why Carnot can scale beyond conventional
  CPUs" (definitive), but the only hardware evidence card is a "KV260 FPGA
  prototype" — prototype ≠ scales-beyond-CPUs.
- Results disclaimer says synthetic pilots are "included only when the card says
  so," yet no result card visibly carries a synthetic-pilot label — the
  promised labeling is absent.
- Two different "0.91" AUROCs (FoVer math-step vs prompt-injection safety) sit
  in different cards with no cue that they measure different things — easy to
  read as one number repeated.
- Typed-constraints numbers (+4.9 pts, 4%→12%) appear in BOTH the capabilities
  bento and as two separate results cards — duplicated.

### Missing essentials
- "Why should I trust the numbers?" is undercut, not supported: the defensive
  provenance paragraph plus jargon makes the evidence harder to trust, not
  easier. No link from a result card to its underlying artifact.
- Maintainer/credibility signal is thin: footer shows a single name ("© 2026
  Ian Blenke"). A stranger may read this as a solo side-project; no team,
  affiliation, or "used by" anchor.
- The result-card meter bars have no legend and don't map to their numbers
  (e.g. "+3.0 points" → 14.6% bar; "+4.9 points" → 66.7% bar). They look
  quantitative but are arbitrary, which erodes rather than builds trust.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — a perfect 1.0 with no sample size or
  anchor.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — 100% on a small, unstated N.
- "Two-GPU parallel retrain — 2.0× speedup, identical losses" — exact 2.0× and
  "identical" read as too clean.
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — a 0.125 AUC baseline is *below* random
  (0.5); to a stranger who knows AUC this looks like a typo or a baseline
  cherry-picked to inflate the delta. This is the single most credibility-
  damaging number on the page.
- "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" rendered with a 95.6%-wide
  green bar — a null result visually dressed as a near-100% win.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: one-sentence "what it does," a concrete 47+28=76
  example, `pip install carnot-ebm`, Apache-2.0, and HuggingFace mirror all in
  the first screen. A stranger gets the pitch immediately.
- "How it works" (Extract → Check → Repair) is clear, jargon-light, and uses
  the same running example — strong narrative spine.
- The page is visibly cleaner than past states: no raw experiment IDs or
  milestone numbers in prose.
